scraped.scraped_description: Contracts for Data Collaboration (C4DC) seeks to strengthen trust, transparency, and accountability of cross-sector data collaboratives. The intent of this initiative is to enable more effective and efficient ways of accessing, sharing and using data for public problem-solving and sustainable development.

name: Contracts for Data Collaboration
tagline: Strengthening trust, transparency, and accountability in cross-sector data collaboratives through legal frameworks and shared resources
sdg_alignment: SDG 16 – Peace, Justice and Strong Institutions
known_funders: Berkman Klein Center for Internet & Society at Harvard University
dependency_risks: Dependent on continued academic institutional support and grant funding; reliance on volunteer contributors
policy_outcomes: Influenced data collaboration frameworks in multiple jurisdictions
Referenced in policy discussions on data governance
outcome_methodology: Case study analysis and stakeholder feedback
documented_limitations: Limited to specific types of data collaboratives
curation_criteria: Legal frameworks and best practices for data collaboratives; focus on trust, transparency, and accountability
government_partnerships: Collaboration with government agencies on data governance frameworks
political_relevance_summary: Tackles opacity in government operations by enabling public access to government data and processes.

movement_building_utility.notes: Provides evidence and data that amplifies advocacy and accountability efforts.

generalizability_notes: Open-source codebase facilitates replication and adaptation. Already deployed across multiple jurisdictions (4 countries), demonstrating cross-context adaptability.
